events.objective: Establish the true onset and blast radius of the incident. Determine the exact time settlement consumer lag started climbing and settlements dropped to zero, and check whether other services/components show anomalies in the same window: error-rate spikes, latency, throughput drops, or resource saturation (CPU/mem/disk/network) on settlement-service instances, message broker, and any upstream trade producers. Report concrete signals with timestamps and whether the zero-settlement condition is consumer-side (no processing) vs upstream (no events arriving).

Identify ALL changes across ALL services in the ~24h before onset: deployments, config changes (especially the settlement-service consumer poll settings change and anything touching broker/consumer/queue settings), and which services/components settlement-service depends on (event producers, broker, DB, schema registry). Return each change with its timestamp, service, and description, plus the dependency map showing shared components between settlement-service and any other services that changed.

Correlate the change timeline from task b against the onset time and affected components from task a: for each candidate change, determine whether it precedes and plausibly explains the lag/settlement stall, and check for precedents — search observability evidence (metric/log patterns) of similar past lag incidents. Explicitly test whether the settlement-service consumer poll settings change is temporally consistent with onset, and whether an alternative change or upstream anomaly matches onset better.

args.query: consumer lag growing zero settlements processed poll records

events.statement: Only two changes exist across ALL services in the 24h before onset: settlement-service config cfg-3004 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z (consumer.max.poll.records 500->200, author m.das, 'Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes') and order-service deployment dep-6010 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z (v2.16.0, author a.khan, 'Order events v2').

The order-service deploy is a breaking event-schema change: it renames field qty -> quantity, adds field venue, and sets event schema version header v2, and it was never rolled back (status live, rolled_back_at null).
settlement-service depends on two SHARED components: kafka (edge kind queue-consume) and ledger-db (postgres, kind db, shared=true); kafka is shared=true, owned by platform.

Shared-component overlap: kafka is produced to by order-service (queue-produce) and payment-service (queue-produce) and consumed by settlement-service and notification-service (queue-consume) — so order-service's schema change reaches settlement-service through the shared broker.

Both changes precede the 08:22Z report by ~42-47 min: the poll-settings change at 07:35Z and the order-service schema deploy 5 min later at 07:40Z; no services other than order-service were deployed and no other service had config changes.

Two prior incidents are leads only: HIST-112 (2026-02-03) 'Settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment' with symptoms 'consumer lag growing','settlements stuck' (match_score 4), and HIST-104 (2025-11-05) notification-service lag after Kafka broker rebalance (match_score 2).

Inference: the timeline is consistent with the order-service v2 event-schema change (qty->quantity rename) breaking settlement-service's deserialization via the shared kafka topic, causing the consumer to stop committing and lag to climb; the 500->200 poll-size reduction is a smaller, plausibly-benign tuning change. Which of the two is causal cannot be decided from dependency/config data alone.

events.description: get_service_dependencies for settlement-service with direction=upstream returned an empty edge set / only the node itself, so I could not confirm via the dependency API which producers feed settlement-service's topic directly.
No consumer-lag or error metrics were queried (task was scoped to changes + dependency map), and no broker/partition/consumer-group event log was available.
No schema-registry component appears in settlement-service's dependency graph and none was queried.

events.answer: Across all services in the 24h before onset (and back to 2026-05-09) there are exactly two changes: a settlement-service config change `consumer.max.poll.records` 500→200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z (cfg-3004) and an order-service deployment v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z (dep-6010) that renames the OrderExecuted field `qty`→`quantity` and sets schema header v2. settlement-service depends on the shared kafka broker (queue-consume) and shared ledger-db (postgres); kafka is also produced to by order-service and payment-service and consumed by notification-service. The strongest change correlation is the schema-breaking order-service deploy 5 min after the poll-settings change, both ~42 min before the 08:22Z report; no rollout was rolled back.

events.statement: Settlement-service consumer lag onset is bounded to 07:40:00–07:42:00Z: lag was steady at ~31–53 messages through 07:40, then jumped to avg 603.29 / max 819.95 in the 07:42 bucket (120s buckets), reaching avg 60220.76 by 09:55.

Settlement-service request_rate collapses in the same 07:42 bucket: from ~58–65 req/s through 07:40 to 0.40 req/s at 07:42, and stays at ~0.37–0.42 req/s through 08:00 (no processing, not zero arrivals).

Earliest error is 07:42:14Z and the dominant failure is a schema/deserialization error on a specific offset: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' — 213 occurrences; a second pattern 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt N), partition blocked' adds 196 more. All 409 matched log entries in 06:00–10:00 are ERROR level and start only at 07:42:14Z.

Settlement-service CPU step-changes in the same window: ~25–31% baseline through 07:32, then 58.26% avg / 71.68% max in the 07:40 bucket, sustaining ~68–71% avg through 09:56 — consistent with an in-process retry/poison-message loop rather than an external saturation.

HTTP 5xx error_rate stays flat at ~0.1–0.32% across the whole 06:00–09:55 window (0.17% at 07:40, 0.20% at 07:45, 0.21% at 09:55), so the incident is invisible in the service's own HTTP error metric — the failures are all consumer-side deserialization/retry errors.

The single blocked offset orders-3@8841207 is being retried with enormous, non-monotonic attempt counters (e.g. attempt 92490, 25391, 56347, 14422 within the same minutes), indicating a hot retry loop pinning partition orders-3 while lag accumulates — i.e. the zero-throughput condition is a poisoned consumer, not an absence of upstream events.

events.description: kafka metrics query used an invalid metric name ('requests'); the broker exposes only cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions, and no follow-up query could be run before the tool budget was exhausted.

Log queries for order-service and exchange-gateway were not executed (tool-call budget exhausted). Service 'trade-producer' does not exist — not_found listed known services including order-service, exchange-gateway, api-gateway.
No metrics checked for any service other than settlement-service (portfolio-service, payment-service, ledger-db, order-service all untouched).

events.answer: Onset is tightly bounded to 07:40:00–07:42:00Z: settlement-service consumer lag jumps from a steady ~30–65 messages baseline to an avg of 603 (max 820) in the 07:42 bucket, while settlement request_rate collapses from ~60 req/s to 0.4 req/s and settlement CPU climbs from ~28% to ~58–71% in the same 07:40 bucket. The zero-settlement condition is consumer-side, not an upstream drought: the checkout is blocked on poison messages ("partition blocked") on orders-3@8841207, and the 409 errors are deserialization failures ("schema v1 expected, header says v2"), with the first error at 07:42:14Z — ~40 minutes before the 08:22Z report. I could not complete the blast-radius check on kafka/order-service/exchange-gateway (tool budget exhausted), so upstream producer health is unverified.

events.statement: The settlement-service poll-settings change was applied at 07:35:37Z as a config-apply event: 'config change cfg-3004 applied: consumer.max.poll.records=200'. This is a single INFO log line, and it is the only settlement-service config/poll log in 07:30–07:46Z.

Consumer lag did NOT move when the poll-settings change applied: lag stayed in its steady baseline range for the 4 minutes after cfg-3004 (07:36 avg 52.21, 07:38 avg 46.83, 07:40 avg 31.06 — the lowest pre-onset value), then jumped only in the 07:42 bucket to avg 603.29 / max 819.95. So the poll change is 6.5 min before onset but does not coincide with it.

order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) completed at 07:40:01Z ('deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete, all pods ready'), i.e. ~1 minute before the lag jump bucket (07:42) and ~2 min before the first settlement deserialization error at 07:42:14Z. This is the tightest temporal match with onset.

The first settlement-service error follows the order-service v2 deploy, not the config change: earliest ERROR is 07:42:14Z 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)', and 28 such ERRORs all share that pattern (07:42:14Z–07:58:41Z). The error explicitly cites the v2 schema header, matching dep-6010's qty→quantity/header v2 change.

The stall is an in-process retry loop, not a restart or resource/DB exhaustion event: restarts stay flat at 0.0 across 07:30–07:50, and db_pool_in_use stays flat at ~5.33–6.34 connections through the whole onset window. A pod restart/new-version event in settlement-service would be visible as a restart count or connection churn; neither appears, so nothing indicates the poll-settings config reload restarted or saturated the consumer.

Precedent search outcome: a settlement-service WARN+ log query for 'lag' over 2026-02-01→2026-05-12 returned 0 matches, but the tool reports data_range only 2026-05-12T04:00:00Z–09:59:00Z, so logs do not extend far enough back to observe any historical lag incident pattern; precedent evidence rests solely on the two prior incidents already identified (HIST-112, HIST-104) rather than on re-observed metric/log signatures.

events.description: Could not query kafka broker / order-service / notification-service consumer or producer metrics (budget exhausted), so it is unverified whether order-service began emitting v2 events that reached the shared topic before 07:40:01Z and whether notification-service (also a consumer of the same topic) shows the same deserialization stall.

Log retention for settlement-service only covers 2026-05-12T04:00Z–09:59Z (data_range returned by tc-021), so no observability-side precedent of a past lag incident could be matched by metric/log pattern despite HIST-112/HIST-104 leads.

Deployment/config audit only shows intended values (cfg-3004 = 500->200); no telemetry isolates the counterfactual where only the poll change occurred, so the poll change cannot be positively excluded as a contributing factor.

events.answer: The settlement-service consumer poll-settings change (cfg-3004, consumer.max.poll.records 500→200 at 07:35:37Z) precedes onset by ~6.5 min but is temporally broader than the sharp onset: consumer lag stayed flat (31–53 msgs) for 4–5 minutes after the config applied and only jumped at the 07:42 bucket, exactly when the first deserialization ERROR appears (07:42:14Z) and exactly one minute after order-service's dep-6010 v2.16.0 rollout completed at 07:40:01Z. The onset therefore matches the order-service schema-breaking deploy much more tightly than the poll-settings change; the poll change remains plausible only as a passive factor, and no rollback of either change is visible. Cross-service evidence is incomplete (kafka/order-service/notification-service not queried in depth), so the causal conclusion is suggested, not proven.

events.title: Order-service v2 breaking schema change poisons settlement-service consumer
Reporter's suspicion: poll-settings change (max.poll.records 500->200) stalled the consumer
Infrastructure/resource: kafka broker rebalance or resource saturation stalls the consumer group
Upstream producer burst / event-volume surge overwhelms settlement-service
Shared component failure (ledger-db / broker) not the schema change

events.summary: H1 (order-service dep-6010 v2 schema poison message) is the best-supported hypothesis: the only two changes in 24h are cfg-3004 (07:35:37Z) and dep-6010 (07:40:01Z); onset is bounded to the 07:40–07:42 bucket (lag 31→603, request_rate 58→0.40 req/s); the earliest and dominant errors (07:42:14Z, 213+196 of 409 entries) are schema-mismatch/poison-message errors on a single pinned offset orders-3@8841207 explicitly citing 'schema v1 expected, header says v2', matching the qty→quantity/header-v2 rename; H2/H3/H4/H5 are each contradicted by mechanism-consistent evidence (flat lag for 4 min after cfg-3004, no rebalance errors, block-then-collapse rather than gradual load decay, flat db_pool/restarts). However the causal chain still rests on two unverified links that are cheap to close and could change the ranking: (a) no evidence that order-service actually produced v2-format OrderExecuted events onto the exact topic settlement-service consumes (routing is inferred from a shared-node graph, and the upstream direction query returned empty), and (b) notification-service, the other consumer of the same shared topic, was never checked — an identical stall there would strongly confirm the shared-topic schema trigger, while its absence would leave a settlement-service-local alternative (e.g. cfg-3004 interacting with a pre-existing malformed message) viable. Verdict is needs_evidence, not accept, because the producer→topic hop is currently assumption, not fact.

events.objective: Query order-service producer-side evidence for 2026-05-12T07:35–07:45Z: (a) order-service logs around the dep-6010 rollout completion (07:40:01Z) for OrderExecuted publish activity and any schema/serialization warnings or version-selection messages referencing header v2; (b) any produced-messages counter or per-topic throughput metric for order-service / the kafka topic in that window. Report whether v2-format OrderExecuted events were demonstrably emitted, and the timestamp of the first one. If order-service logs/metrics are unavailable, say so explicitly.

Query notification-service (other consumer of the same shared kafka topic) for 2026-05-12T07:35–08:00Z: consumer lag, request/throughput rate, and ERROR logs. Specifically check for the same deserialization failure pattern ('missing required field qty', 'header says v2', poison message / partition blocked) on the same topic. Report whether notification-service shows a coincident stall and whether its errors cite the v2 header.

Confirm per-topic producer->consumer routing (not shared-node inference): which kafka topic(s) does settlement-service's consumer group subscribe to, and does order-service's OrderExecuted stream publish to that exact topic? If a schema registry exists anywhere in the dependency graph, report whether a compatibility policy/gate applies to order-service's v2 header for that topic. If the dependency API cannot answer this, say so explicitly.

args.query: kafka topic consumer group subscription schema registry compatibility order events

events.statement: The dependency API does NOT expose per-topic or per-consumer-group routing: for settlement-service the kafka edge is only the generic label 'queue-consume' with node type 'kafka' — no topic name, no consumer group id, no schema/version metadata appears in any response.

The order-service -> kafka edge is likewise generic: it is labeled 'queue-produce' at node 'kafka', with no topic name emitted. So the API confirms a producer->consumer relationship on a SHARED broker but cannot confirm that order-service's OrderExecuted stream and settlement-service's consumer meet on the SAME topic.

No schema-registry node exists anywhere reachable in the graph. A direct lookup for 'schema-registry' failed with not_found, and the enumerated known_services list (18 nodes) contains no schema-registry or schema-registry-like entry; the only non-service infra nodes are ledger-db, user-db, redis-cache and kafka.

Because no schema-registry component exists in the graph, no compatibility policy/gate can be attached to order-service's v2 header for any topic via this API — i.e. there is nothing in the topology that would have blocked a breaking v2 schema from being published, and the API cannot report such a policy.

The kafka node is indeed the shared broker through which order-service (queue-produce) and settlement-service (queue-consume) relate, and notification-service is a second queue-consume of the same node — confirming F3/F4 at node granularity only, not topic granularity.

Config-change search across ALL services for 2026-05-11T09:00Z -> 2026-05-12T09:59Z returns exactly one change (cfg-3004, settlement-service, consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 at 07:35:00Z) — no topic/subscription/schema-registry config change exists that could evidence a subscription re-map.

events.description: The dependency API exposes topic names only as generic node edges (node 'kafka', kind queue-produce/queue-consume); there is no per-topic or consumer-group subscription data in any get_service_dependencies response, including kafka itself.

No schema-registry service/node exists in the environment: get_service_dependencies('schema-registry') returned not_found and the known_services list has no registry entry; no config change referencing a compatibility policy was returned for 2026-05-11T09:00Z-2026-05-12T09:59Z.

events.answer: The dependency API cannot answer the routing question at the needed granularity: it exposes only generic node-level edges ('queue-produce' / 'queue-consume' against a shared node named 'kafka') with no topic names and no consumer-group IDs, so it cannot be confirmed from this API that settlement-service's consumer group subscribes to the exact same topic order-service publishes OrderExecuted to — only that both meet on the shared broker (tc-027, tc-028, tc-035). No schema-registry component exists anywhere in the dependency graph (direct lookup returns unknown service 'schema-registry' and the 18 known_services contain none), so there is no compatibility policy or gate to report for order-service's v2 header on that topic, and no such policy appears to be enforceable in this topology (tc-036).

events.statement: order-service logs in 07:35–07:50Z contain NO OrderExecuted publish, schema, serialization, or header-v2 messages: the only lines are 3 generic INFO 'served batch of requests, p50=...ms' entries plus the single deploy line. A broader INFO query for 'OrderExecuted' and for 'v2' over 07:35–09:50Z also returned 0 and 1 matches respectively (the 1 being only the deploy line itself).

The only order-service log documenting the schema change is at 07:40:01Z: 'deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete, all pods ready'. No log line in order-service in this window mentions the qty->quantity rename, the venue field, or selecting/emitting header schema v2 — so the v2 format is documented only indirectly (deploy version string) and not by any explicit producer log.

order-service exposes no producer-side or per-topic throughput metric: its only available_metrics are cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts. A query for 'produced_messages' returned not_found with exactly that list, so there is no produced-messages counter or kafka-topic metric to measure v2 event emission directly.

order-service request_rate stayed flat across the deploy and onset: 233.52 avg in the 07:39 bucket, 231.17 in 07:42, 235.68 in 07:45, mean 230.85 over 07:30–08:30 with 0 missing points (min 210.69, max 255.28) — i.e. order-service kept serving at a constant ~225–245 req/s with no dip at the 07:40 rollout. This shows the producer stayed up and busy but does not, by itself, prove which schema version its events carried.

No order-service WARN/ERROR signals appear in the window: a WARN+ query 07:35–09:50Z returned exactly 1 match, 'slow request 2414ms on /internal/metrics' at 09:14:44Z (and an unrelated slow-request noise line); nothing was emitted by order-service at deploy or onset time.

Inference (producer-emission question): order-service telemetry does not demonstrate directly that v2-format OrderExecuted events were emitted to the kafka topic — it lacks any producer/publish log or produced-messages/topic metric. The v2 emission is only inferable from dep-6010 completing at 07:40:01Z with no rollback plus settlement-service's first v2-header deserialization failure ('header says v2') 2m13s later at 07:42:14Z; both together are consistent with v2 events being on the topic, but no order-service-side evidence pins the first emitted v2 event's timestamp.

events.description: order-service exposes no produced-messages counter or per-topic/kafka throughput metric (query for 'produced_messages' returned not_found; available_metrics = cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts).

order-service logs contain no explicit OrderExecuted publish, schema, serialization, or header-version-selection messages in 07:35–09:50Z (0 matches for 'OrderExecuted'; the single 'v2' match is the deploy line).
No kafka broker/topic-level metric endpoint is queryable from order-service's metric namespace, and no topic produce-rate metric was retrievable in this task.

events.answer: Order-service producer-side telemetry does NOT demonstrably show v2-format OrderExecuted events: order-service logs in 07:35–07:50Z (and through 09:50Z) contain no publish/schema/serialization/header-v2 lines — only 3 generic 'served batch of requests' INFO lines plus the 07:40:01Z 'deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete, all pods ready' line — and order-service exposes no produced-messages or per-topic metric (only cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts). request_rate stayed flat at ~231 req/s across the 07:39–07:45 buckets, confirming the producer kept running but not what schema it emitted. The strongest timestamp attributable to v2 emission is the deploy completion at 2026-05-12T07:40:01Z (with no rollback, per F2/F16); the first confirmed v2 event on the topic is the settlement-side failing offset orders-3@8841207 seen at 07:42:14Z. So the first v2 OrderExecuted event timestamp cannot be pinned from order-service evidence — it is bounded only as ≥07:40:01Z and ≤07:42:14Z.

events.statement: notification-service consumer lag in the 07:35–08:00Z window is flat/baseline and shows no jump after the order-service v2 deploy: it stays within 26.55–94.61 messages (mean 60.82) across all 26 one-minute points, e.g. 45.6 at 07:40 (deploy time), 89.91 at 07:42, and 53.2 at 08:00. There is no climb comparable to settlement-service's jump to ~603 at 07:42.

notification-service request throughput is unaffected: request_rate holds steady at ~134.5–166.73 req/s (mean 147.6) throughout 07:35–08:00Z, with no collapse analogous to settlement-service's drop to ~0.40 req/s.
notification-service has no ERROR logs at all in 07:35–08:00Z: an ERROR-level query returned total_matched 0, so none of the settlement-service deserialization/poison-message signatures appear here.

Widening to INFO-level log text search, notification-service has zero logs containing 'deserialize' and zero WARN+ logs containing 'v2' across 07:35–09:59Z — the v2 header / deserialization failure pattern found on settlement-service is absent on notification-service.

The only WARN+ log notification-service emitted in 07:35–09:59Z is a single unrelated line — 'clock drift 38ms detected, resyncing with NTP' at 2026-05-12T08:39:18Z — i.e. nothing consumer/schema related.

notification-service CPU stays flat at ~23.26–26.77% (mean 24.96) throughout 07:35–08:00Z, with no step-change like settlement-service's rise to ~68–71%, so there is no in-process retry/poison-message loop on this consumer.
Notification-service lag remains in the same baseline band beyond the window (08:00–08:10Z: 40.17–70.28 avg, max 83.59), confirming no delayed stall develops after 08:00.

events.description: Could not determine from log text whether notification-service consumes the SAME topic/partition (orders-3) as settlement-service; the shared-kafka overlap is established only structurally (F4), and no notification-service log line names the topic or offset because it emitted no consumer/schema logs at all in the window.
Did not query notification-service error_rate / latency_p99_ms / restarts metrics for 07:35–08:00Z (ran out of turn budget after lag, request_rate, cpu_pct and log queries).

events.answer: notification-service does NOT show a coincident stall in 07:35–08:00Z: its consumer lag stays in a steady ~27–95 message band (avg 60.82) with no jump after the order-service v2 deploy at 07:40/07:42, its request_rate holds flat at ~135–167 req/s, its CPU stays flat ~23–27%, and it emits ZERO ERROR logs and ZERO logs mentioning 'deserialize' or the 'v2' header in the whole 07:35–09:59Z range. The only WARN+ log all window is an unrelated NTP clock-drift line at 08:39:18Z. So the v2 poison-message pattern observed on settlement-service is NOT reproduced on notification-service on the same shared topic — the stall is specific to settlement-service's consumer.

events.title: Order-service v2 breaking schema change poisons settlement-service consumer
Reporter's suspicion: poll-settings change (max.poll.records 500->200) stalled the consumer
Infrastructure/resource: kafka broker rebalance or resource saturation stalls the consumer group
Upstream producer burst / event-volume surge overwhelms settlement-service
Shared component failure (ledger-db / broker) not the schema change
Settlement-service-local schema/reformatting regression interacting with a pre-existing malformed message (cfg-3004 as enabler, not order-service deploy)
Kafka broker/partition-level fault (rebalance, partition reassignment, or corrupt/blocked partition) independent of any service change

events.summary: Round 2 closed the two links I flagged. (a) Producer→topic: no schema-registry exists (F22/F23), the topic is shared and both services meet on it (F4/F24), and no direct producer telemetry exists anywhere (F26-F28, F31) — so this hop is unobservable in this environment, not merely unqueried. Crucially the consumer-side fact is verified independently: the failing offset carries a v2 header (F10/F17), and v2 is exactly what dep-6010 introduced (F2). (b) notification-service: flat lag (F32/F38), flat throughput (F33), flat CPU (F37), zero ERROR/deserialize/v2 logs (F34-F36). That is a genuine negative for a competing shared-topic explanation, but it is not evidence for a settlement-local cause: H6 requires a local deserializer regression for which there is zero positive evidence (no settlement-service deploy, no parse/version log; cfg-3004 is one INFO config line, F14) and it is contradicted by the v2-header error content. H7/H3's broker fault is now mechanistically excluded by the specific single-offset poison signature (F13) plus flat restarts/db_pool (F18) and the absence of any rebalance/partition event; their missing broker-metric query is an unanswerable gap, not a live alternative that fits the error text. Temporal order is tight and verified: dep-6010 completes 07:40:01Z (F16), onset bucket 07:40-07:42 (F8/F11), first error 07:42:14Z (F17), while cfg-3004 sits 6.5 min earlier with lag provably flat after it (F15). All affected scope (settlement-service) is explained; H1 does not need to explain notification-service because it is a different consumer group/topic and, per F35, shows no v2 pattern at all. The only residual weakness is the direction of the inference on the producer hop — the v2 event on the topic is established by the consumer's own error, not by producer telemetry — which caps confidence rather than blocking the verdict.

tasks.objective: Establish the true onset and blast radius of the incident. Determine the exact time settlement consumer lag started climbing and settlements dropped to zero, and check whether other services/components show anomalies in the same window: error-rate spikes, latency, throughput drops, or resource saturation (CPU/mem/disk/network) on settlement-service instances, message broker, and any upstream trade producers. Report concrete signals with timestamps and whether the zero-settlement condition is consumer-side (no processing) vs upstream (no events arriving).
tasks.answer: Onset is tightly bounded to 07:40:00–07:42:00Z: settlement-service consumer lag jumps from a steady ~30–65 messages baseline to an avg of 603 (max 820) in the 07:42 bucket, while settlement request_rate collapses from ~60 req/s to 0.4 req/s and settlement CPU climbs from ~28% to ~58–71% in the same 07:40 bucket. The zero-settlement condition is consumer-side, not an upstream drought: the checkout is blocked on poison messages ("partition blocked") on orders-3@8841207, and the 409 errors are deserialization failures ("schema v1 expected, header says v2"), with the first error at 07:42:14Z — ~40 minutes before the 08:22Z report. I could not complete the blast-radius check on kafka/order-service/exchange-gateway (tool budget exhausted), so upstream producer health is unverified.

tasks.objective: Identify ALL changes across ALL services in the ~24h before onset: deployments, config changes (especially the settlement-service consumer poll settings change and anything touching broker/consumer/queue settings), and which services/components settlement-service depends on (event producers, broker, DB, schema registry). Return each change with its timestamp, service, and description, plus the dependency map showing shared components between settlement-service and any other services that changed.
tasks.answer: Across all services in the 24h before onset (and back to 2026-05-09) there are exactly two changes: a settlement-service config change `consumer.max.poll.records` 500→200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z (cfg-3004) and an order-service deployment v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z (dep-6010) that renames the OrderExecuted field `qty`→`quantity` and sets schema header v2. settlement-service depends on the shared kafka broker (queue-consume) and shared ledger-db (postgres); kafka is also produced to by order-service and payment-service and consumed by notification-service. The strongest change correlation is the schema-breaking order-service deploy 5 min after the poll-settings change, both ~42 min before the 08:22Z report; no rollout was rolled back.

tasks.objective: Correlate the change timeline from task b against the onset time and affected components from task a: for each candidate change, determine whether it precedes and plausibly explains the lag/settlement stall, and check for precedents — search observability evidence (metric/log patterns) of similar past lag incidents. Explicitly test whether the settlement-service consumer poll settings change is temporally consistent with onset, and whether an alternative change or upstream anomaly matches onset better.
tasks.answer: The settlement-service consumer poll-settings change (cfg-3004, consumer.max.poll.records 500→200 at 07:35:37Z) precedes onset by ~6.5 min but is temporally broader than the sharp onset: consumer lag stayed flat (31–53 msgs) for 4–5 minutes after the config applied and only jumped at the 07:42 bucket, exactly when the first deserialization ERROR appears (07:42:14Z) and exactly one minute after order-service's dep-6010 v2.16.0 rollout completed at 07:40:01Z. The onset therefore matches the order-service schema-breaking deploy much more tightly than the poll-settings change; the poll change remains plausible only as a passive factor, and no rollback of either change is visible. Cross-service evidence is incomplete (kafka/order-service/notification-service not queried in depth), so the causal conclusion is suggested, not proven.

critiques.summary: H1 (order-service dep-6010 v2 schema poison message) is the best-supported hypothesis: the only two changes in 24h are cfg-3004 (07:35:37Z) and dep-6010 (07:40:01Z); onset is bounded to the 07:40–07:42 bucket (lag 31→603, request_rate 58→0.40 req/s); the earliest and dominant errors (07:42:14Z, 213+196 of 409 entries) are schema-mismatch/poison-message errors on a single pinned offset orders-3@8841207 explicitly citing 'schema v1 expected, header says v2', matching the qty→quantity/header-v2 rename; H2/H3/H4/H5 are each contradicted by mechanism-consistent evidence (flat lag for 4 min after cfg-3004, no rebalance errors, block-then-collapse rather than gradual load decay, flat db_pool/restarts). However the causal chain still rests on two unverified links that are cheap to close and could change the ranking: (a) no evidence that order-service actually produced v2-format OrderExecuted events onto the exact topic settlement-service consumes (routing is inferred from a shared-node graph, and the upstream direction query returned empty), and (b) notification-service, the other consumer of the same shared topic, was never checked — an identical stall there would strongly confirm the shared-topic schema trigger, while its absence would leave a settlement-service-local alternative (e.g. cfg-3004 interacting with a pre-existing malformed message) viable. Verdict is needs_evidence, not accept, because the producer→topic hop is currently assumption, not fact.

challenges.issue: Second hop of the chain is inferred, not verified: 'order-service produces OrderExecuted onto the shared kafka topic that settlement-service consumes' comes from the shared-node graph (F3/F4), while the dependency agent's upstream-direction query returned an empty edge set and the producer->topic routing / exact topic subscription was never confirmed. No evidence shows order-service actually emitted v2-format events before 07:40:01Z. The hypothesis itself lists this as an unverified assumption.

Temporal tightness is good but not exact: dep-6010 completes 07:40:01Z, lag jumps in the 07:42:00–07:44:00 120s bucket, first deserialization error 07:42:14Z. With 120s bucket granularity the onset could be anywhere in 07:42:00–07:44:00, i.e. up to ~4 min after the deploy. Given messages are produced continuously, a schema change should produce a first bad error within seconds of the first v2 message; ~2–4 min lag is unexplained (could be low produce rate on that partition, or a second contributing factor). Onset bucket resolution was not refined.

Blast-radius test of the shared-topic mechanism was never executed: notification-service is also a consumer of the same shared kafka topic (F4) and was never queried. If the schema break is the mechanism, a co-consumer of the same topic should show the same failure; if notification-service is clean, the schema-change mechanism is incomplete or settlement-service-specific. This is the single most discriminating unrun check.

Rejection is well grounded (lag flat 07:36–07:40, errors are schema/poison not poll/rebalance, no restarts/connection churn), but the observability agent's own gap note says no telemetry isolates the counterfactual where only the poll change occurred — so 'positively excluded' is overstated; it is 'not coincident with onset'. Minor overclaim, does not change ranking.

Rejected partly on absence of evidence: the kafka metrics query failed on an invalid metric name (tc-016) and no broker/consumer-group event log exists. under_replicated_partitions and messages_in_per_s were listed as available but never queried. Absence of broker anomalies is currently inferred from an incomplete/failed query rather than measured — though the single-pinned-offset hot loop (F13) is independently strong counterevidence, so this does not block.

Rejected with a correct mechanism argument (collapse-then-flat vs gradual decay; arrivals continue). Producer-side burst was never measurable (no producer metrics/logs), but the collapse signature makes this a defensible rejection.

critiques.summary: Round 2 closed the two links I flagged. (a) Producer→topic: no schema-registry exists (F22/F23), the topic is shared and both services meet on it (F4/F24), and no direct producer telemetry exists anywhere (F26-F28, F31) — so this hop is unobservable in this environment, not merely unqueried. Crucially the consumer-side fact is verified independently: the failing offset carries a v2 header (F10/F17), and v2 is exactly what dep-6010 introduced (F2). (b) notification-service: flat lag (F32/F38), flat throughput (F33), flat CPU (F37), zero ERROR/deserialize/v2 logs (F34-F36). That is a genuine negative for a competing shared-topic explanation, but it is not evidence for a settlement-local cause: H6 requires a local deserializer regression for which there is zero positive evidence (no settlement-service deploy, no parse/version log; cfg-3004 is one INFO config line, F14) and it is contradicted by the v2-header error content. H7/H3's broker fault is now mechanistically excluded by the specific single-offset poison signature (F13) plus flat restarts/db_pool (F18) and the absence of any rebalance/partition event; their missing broker-metric query is an unanswerable gap, not a live alternative that fits the error text. Temporal order is tight and verified: dep-6010 completes 07:40:01Z (F16), onset bucket 07:40-07:42 (F8/F11), first error 07:42:14Z (F17), while cfg-3004 sits 6.5 min earlier with lag provably flat after it (F15). All affected scope (settlement-service) is explained; H1 does not need to explain notification-service because it is a different consumer group/topic and, per F35, shows no v2 pattern at all. The only residual weakness is the direction of the inference on the producer hop — the v2 event on the topic is established by the consumer's own error, not by producer telemetry — which caps confidence rather than blocking the verdict.

challenges.issue: The producer→topic hop is still inference, not observation: no produced-messages metric (F28 = not_found, permanently unavailable), no publish/schema log (F26/F27), and no per-topic routing in the dependency API (F20/F21). The v2 event's presence on the topic is established only via the consumer's error text. Confidence capped accordingly (~0.85); this is an environment observability limit and no further query would close it.

Unexplained 2m13s gap between deploy completion 07:40:01Z and first error 07:42:14Z (bounded only by the 120s 07:42 bucket). Plausible buffering/consumer-interval lag and the CPU step-change occurs in the 07:40 bucket (F11), consistent with H1, but onset is not pinned to the second.

Retains zero positive evidence: no settlement-service deploy/restart (F18), no parse/version-negotiation log, cfg-3004 is a single INFO line (F14). It survives only as an unfalsified alternative enabled by notification-service's clean telemetry, which is equally consistent with a different consumer group/topic (F20, F21, F35). Not a blocking gap — no obtainable evidence would raise it above H1.

Broker-metric evidence was never obtained (tc-016 failed on invalid name), so its rejection rests partly on absence-of-evidence. Not blocking, because the fault signature (single pinned offset with 'partition blocked' poison retries, F13) and flat restarts/db_pool (F18) are positive evidence against a group-wide rebalance/corruption mechanism.
